subject: general
question:
The pie chart given below shows the number of bike sold by 8 different companies. The total number of bike sold by all these 8 companies are 2000. Number of bikes sold by a particular company is shown as a percent of total number of bike sold by all these 8 companies.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/097b2c0c7cc232804a08e1223b93f646c812dd051707985fdaa566dcac6a6d2d.png] 

What is the difference between the average number of bikes sold by P, Q, R and S and the average number of bikes sold by T, U, V and W?
solution:
Calculation:

The average number of bikes sold by P, Q, R and S = {(21 + 19 + 5 + 20)% × 2000} ÷ 4 = 325

So, the average number of bikes sold by T, U, V, and W = (2000 - 1300)/4 = 175

Now, the difference = 325 - 175 = 150

**∴ The difference between the average number of bikes sold by P, Q, R and S and the average number of bikes sold by T, U, V and W is 150.**
